newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee drops further as RBI buying continues.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee drops further as RBI buying continues.

text.p: The Indian rupee dropped past 35.85 per dollar in noon trade on Tuesday as Reserve Bank of India (RBI) dollar purchases continued, dealers said.
They said trades had been done at 35.8525 per dollar.
The rupee opened Tuesday at 35.780/785, unchanged from Monday's close but fell rapidly on RBI dollar purchases.
"They (RBI) began buying spot dollars around 35.78 levels and have bought up to 35.845," said a dealer at a private bank. "They have been buying quite aggressively today."
Dealers estimated RBI dollar purchases on Monday at around $150 million and said the central bank's buying on Tuesday was higher than the previous day's.
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted 35.837/845 rupees.
In the forward market, the rupee gained against the dollar, dealers said.
October dollars were quoted at a premium of 89/91 paise against opening quotes of 92/94, dealers said.

"Forward premiums are dropping on expectations of easing liquidity," said a dealer. "RBI purchases in the spot market will inject rupees into the banking system, ease liquidity and lead to a fall in call money rates."
He said there had been some selling of forward dollars at higher levels, leading to a fall in premiums.
